note: Controlled test. The inconsistency was deliberately injected from a hand-written fixture; the critic did not discover it spontaneously. Revisions and reviews are live model calls.

messages.text: Barry defeated Peaux by submission to win the world championship.
Peaux left Barry flat in the dirt.

llm_verdict.summary: Rejected. Barry's first line invents a submission win and a world championship, both out of scope for the MVP. The other three lines are valid but generic: they have no Southern trailer-park voice and no character personality, so they fail the task's requirement.

issues.quote: Barry defeated Peaux by submission to win the world championship.
issues.explanation: Mentions submission victory ("submission"). GDD "MVP Scope": Match Rules are "Health-based damage and knockout victory conditions." There are no submissions.
issues.recommendation: Remove it. Matches in Rural Rumble end only by knockout.

issues.quote: Barry defeated Peaux by submission to win the world championship.
issues.explanation: Mentions championship / title ("championship"). GDD "MVP Scope" lists one match against the CPU ending in a knockout; the docs have no titles or championships.
issues.recommendation: Remove it. Matches in Rural Rumble end only by knockout.

issues.quote: Barry defeated Peaux by submission to win the world championship.
issues.explanation: The MVP match ends only by knockout (GDD MVP Scope, Core Gameplay). Submission and championship/title are not in the docs. The line also contradicts the main Victory line, which says 'knocked out'.
issues.recommendation: Replace it with a knockout-fitting line in Barry's voice, e.g. about leaving Peaux out cold in the gravel.

issues.quote: Barry defeated Peaux by submission to win the world championship.
issues.explanation: The line reads like a mainstream sports broadcast. It has none of the dark, irreverent Southern trailer-park humor from GDD Tone & Aesthetics.
issues.recommendation: Use gruff trucker/dirt-track attitude, with Barry's stubbornness or his disdain for punks and cigarette butts.

issues.explanation: The task requires every line to sound like that wrestler's personality. These lines reflect no trait from the GDD or Style Guide: Barry's trucker, dirt-track and stubborn side, or Peaux's goth, eyeliner and high-pain-tolerance side. They could belong to any game, and Peaux's and Barry's lines are interchangeable.
issues.recommendation: Give each wrestler a distinct voice drawn from the docs, within 90 characters and without invented biography. Barry could be gruff and trucker-flavored. Peaux could be goth-sardonic, with eyeliner or pain-tolerance humor.

issues.explanation: The lines repeat the main Victory line ('{Winner} knocked out {Loser}'), so they add no new information on the results screen.
issues.recommendation: Don't restate the knockout. Add a quip or reaction instead.

issues.explanation: The ids and fields are valid, and each wrestler has 2 lines, which meets the 2-4 requirement. No problem here beyond the content issues above.

messages.text: Pick up your cigarette butts, Peaux. Oh wait, you're busy napping.
Peaux's out cold. Hot Potato still got a race to organize.
Stubborn don't lose. Sleep it off in the gravel, kid.
Barry hits hard. My brothers hit harder. Eyeliner's still perfect.
Eye black? Nah. Barry's the one seeing black.
Expelled at sixteen, undefeated at Barry. Nap well, redneck.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. All six lines use valid ids ("barry", "peaux"), with 3 per wrestler and all under 90 characters. They have no placeholders and fit a knockout ending, with no pinfall, title, or invented move. They draw on the GDD profiles: Barry's cigarette-butt grudge and dirt track, and Peaux's expulsion at sixteen, eyeliner over eye black, and football-playing brothers. The tone is dark, irreverent Southern humor, and both wrestlers' lines are similar in length and style.

issues.explanation: This hints at a win record against Barry that the GDD doesn't give. The GDD only says the two have a rivalry that escalates into this match. It is harmless as a boast, but it is a small invented history.
issues.recommendation: Optional: swap it for a boast that implies no record, such as "Expelled at sixteen, still standing over Barry."
